title: From survival to scale: How Senegal is building a pipeline of growth firms
gist: Senegal's $195 million World Bank JET Program has supported over 8,000 SMEs, formalized 5,000+ firms and backed more than 71,000 jobs by building durable institutions (ADEPME windows, the Oyass SME equity fund, FONGIP guarantees) in an economy where only 1.3% of firms are formal with five or more employees. Logidoo's 21% revenue gain and 86% export growth illustrate the model.

insights.claim: Only 1.3 percent of Senegalese firms are formal with five or more employees, and more than 94 percent of businesses operate informally with low productivity.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Senegal's investable formal corporate base is very small.
insights.locator: To understand what the program set

insights.claim: In the 2025 Enterprise Survey, 23.7 percent of Senegalese companies identified business licensing as a major constraint, nearly double the global average.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Regulatory friction is a material barrier to firm growth in Senegal.

insights.claim: A 2020 World Bank survey of 1,800 Senegalese firms found only 36 percent use a computer, 30 percent a smartphone and 34 percent the internet for business.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Large digitization gap implies upside for business software and connectivity providers.

themes.theme: JET Program design and institutional architecture

insights.claim: Senegal's JET Program launched in 2021 with a $125 million IDA investment and, after $65 million in additional financing approved at end-2025, has a $195 million budget extended to December 2027.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Sizes development-finance support for Senegal's SME sector.

insights.claim: The program created institutions meant to outlast the project cycle, including four SME service windows at ADEPME, a Competitiveness Task Force, a PPP Project Preparation Fund and a strengthened UNAPPP unit.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Durable SME and PPP institutions can improve deal flow for private investors.

insights.claim: FONSIS launched the Oyass Fund in January 2024 as Senegal's first SME-dedicated equity fund, which by end-2025 had a pipeline of 49 projects across 13 sectors needing about €38 million, 27 percent women-led.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: An emerging SME equity pipeline in Senegal for co-investors.

insights.claim: The authors argue supporting individual firms without building the surrounding ecosystem produces limited, short-lived results.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Ecosystem depth matters more than one-off firm subsidies for SME investment outcomes.
insights.quote: supporting individual firms without building the ecosystem around them produces limited and short-lived results.

insights.claim: As of early 2026, the JET Program had supported over 8,000 SMEs through ADEPME matching grants, more than triple the original target of 2,500, with over 40 percent in agribusiness and 52 percent women-owned or managed.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Program reached far beyond targets, suggesting strong SME demand.

insights.claim: The program allocated more than $17.8 million in performance matching grants for technology adoption and mobilized over $26 million in partial credit guarantees through FONGIP, including $3.4 million for women-owned SMEs.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Guarantee schemes de-risk SME lending for Senegalese banks.

insights.claim: The JET Program supported formalization of more than 5,000 companies, and supported businesses created or maintained more than 71,000 jobs per government reports.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Formalization expands the tax and credit base; jobs figures are self-reported by agencies.

insights.claim: Senegalese logistics firm Logidoo, with program support including 75 percent financing of technology development costs and 75 percent of annual rent in Côte d'Ivoire, grew revenue 21.2 percent and export revenue 85.97 percent in one year.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Illustrates how subsidized expansion can quickly scale regional logistics firms in West Africa.

insights.claim: Logidoo's permanent workforce grew from 21 to 57 employees, including 19 women, after expanding to Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Shows job creation potential from SME scaling support.

insights.claim: The additional financing focuses support on sectors and regional poles with the strongest job and export potential, accelerates reforms to business registration and procedures, and links to the upcoming IFC Local Champions Initiative in Senegal.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: IFC capital may flow to Senegalese growth firms graduating from the program.

insights.claim: The World Bank pairs ADEPME services and FONGIP guarantees for de-risking with IFC long-term capital and advisory, such as AgriConnect for agri-finance, under a One World Bank Group approach.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Blended public de-risking plus IFC capital is a template for frontier SME finance.

insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Similar SME programs may roll out in other frontier markets.
